question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer is launching the Himalaya Arbitrage Fund, a Category III AIF with a target corpus of INR 600 crore. For the purpose of sponsor/manager continuing interest, what is the MINIMUM commitment he must make to comply with SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012?

answer.text: INR 10 crore (5% of INR 600 crore = INR 30 crore; INR 10 crore is lower, so INR 10 crore applies)
INR 30 crore (i.e., 5% of corpus, treating it as the higher-of rule)
INR 15 crore (2.5% of corpus as per Cat III rules)
INR 5 crore (absolute minimum irrespective of corpus)

explanation.text: The Logic: For Category III AIFs, sponsor/manager continuing interest is the LOWER of (a) 5% of the corpus or (b) INR 10 crore. 5% of INR 600 cr = INR 30 cr; the lower of INR 30 cr and INR 10 cr is INR 10 crore. The commitment must be made as a fresh investment (not by way of fee waiver or transfer of stocks) and is locked in until investor distributions are complete. The Trap: Option B picks 5% outright and misreads the rule as 'whichever is higher'. Option C confuses Cat III (5%) with Cat I/II (2.5%). Option D invents an absolute floor that does not exist in the regulations. Note: The rule applies on the corpus committed; an upsized corpus does not change the INR 10 crore cap once 5% of corpus exceeds INR 10 crore.
